cards.body:
*Lesson 2.3 · Routers & Filters*

_≈ 90 minutes · with Emeka_

You met branching in Zapier's Paths. Make's version has its own habits: filters can sit on any connection, routes can't join back together, and sometimes you _want_ one order to take several routes at once. Today you build the 8 p.m. "tomorrow's deliveries" run that sorts every order.

*Your problem:* Different orders need different handling, and one path doesn't fit all.
*The plan:* Route bundles with routers and filters, including a fallback route.
*After this lesson:* Your scenarios handle every case, not only the happy one.

*Eight o'clock, every night*

*Every evening:* Tolu reads through tomorrow's orders and sorts them into three jobs. It takes an hour.

*The twist:* Some orders need two jobs at once: a big unpaid order needs a reminder _and_ an alert.

*Glitch:* "In Make, routes split but never rejoin. Enjoy building everything twice!"

*Weave:* "Some of my arms share the work, some take turns. You decide which, on purpose."

*Filters live on the links*

In Make, a filter isn't a module: it sits on the *connection between two modules*. Click the link (the dotted line) and set up a filter. Bundles that fail stop there. Filters use no credits, and the modules after them don't run for the stopped bundles.

- *Operators by type*: Text (equal to, contains, matches pattern), Numeric (greater than, less than or equal), Date (before, after), Array (contains), Basic (exists, does not exist).
- *Case-insensitive options*: Text operators come in case-insensitive versions: "Paid", "paid" and "PAID" all match.
- *AND / OR*: Conditions in one group must all pass (AND); add an OR group for alternatives.
- *Label every filter*: Give it a name like "Only paid orders". It shows on the canvas.

*Routers: one bundle, several routes*

A *Router* module splits the flow into routes. Each route begins with a link, which can carry a filter. A bundle is sent down *every route whose filter it passes*, one route after another in the router's route order. A route marked as the *fallback* receives only bundles that passed no other route. Routers are free of credits.

*Exclusive or additive? Decide on purpose*

*Exclusive routes*

- Each bundle should take exactly one route (like 1.3's order router).
- Write conditions that can't both be true, and add a fallback.
- Test with a truth table.

*Additive routes*

- Each route is an independent rule: "if X, also do this".
- Several can fire for one bundle, and that's correct.
- Make sure no two routes do the _same_ job twice.

*Sage:* Write the rule in words next to each route: "Rider list: every order that will be delivered." If two routes' sentences describe the same job, you have a duplicate. If no sentence covers a case, you need the fallback.

*Routes never merge back*

In Zapier, Paths also end their branches. In Make, once a route splits off, it runs to its own end. If two routes both need the same final step (say, "log to the Activity tab"), you have three options:

- *Repeat the step*: Put the same module at the end of each route. Simple; fine for one or two modules.
- *Do it before the router*: Anything every bundle needs should happen before the split.
- *Call a shared scenario*: For longer shared endings, send the bundle to another scenario (via a webhook) that does the common work once (2.5).

*Route order and nested routers*

- *Route order*: Routes run one after another. If route 1 updates the row and route 2 reads it, the order matters. Use the router's option to set the order.
- *Nested routers*: A route can contain another router. Keep it to two levels; deeper nesting gets hard to read.
- *Empty routes*: A route with a filter and no modules is a clear way to say "do nothing for these" and keeps the fallback from catching them.

cards.body:
*Solved problem: the 8 p.m. tomorrow run*

*The goal.* Every evening at 8 p.m., find all orders for tomorrow and sort them: deliverable orders go on the rider list, unpaid ones get a payment reminder, big ones alert Tolu, and anything strange is flagged. Cancelled orders are ignored.

*Step 1 · Schedule and search*

New scenario. First module: *Google Sheets · Search Rows* on Orders, filter `delivery_date` equal to `{{formatDate(addDays(now; 1); "YYYY-MM-DD")}}`. Schedule: every day at 20:00. (A search as the first module runs on the schedule and returns one bundle per matching order.)

*Step 2 · Filter out cancelled orders on the first link*

Click the link after Search Rows and add a filter labelled *Not cancelled*: `status` · Text operators: Not equal to (case insensitive) · `Cancelled`.

*Step 3 · Add the router and write each rule in words*

_Route · Rule in words · Filter · Module_
- *1 · Rider list* · Every order that will be delivered tomorrow · status = Paid *OR* channel = standing · Sheets · Add a Row to Deliveries
- *2 · Reminder* · Unpaid customer orders get a nudge · status = New *AND* channel ≠ standing · Gmail · Send reminder with payment link
- *3 · Big order* · Tolu hears about every order over ₦50,000 · total (numeric) > 50000 · Telegram or Gmail · Alert Tolu
- *Fallback* · Anything that matched none of the above · Set as fallback route · Sheets · Add a Row to Needs checking

Routes 1–3 are *additive*: a paid big order takes routes 1 and 3; an unpaid big order takes 2 and 3. Nothing is done twice, because each route has a different job.

*Step 4 · Try the design*

Change the order's status, channel and total to see which routes it takes.
Hands-on lab: Try the design. It's interactive, so open it in the app and try it there.

*Step 5 · Test with a truth table of real rows*

_Test order · Status · Channel · Total · Expected routes_
*T1:* Paid · whatsapp · 26,500 · 1
*T2:* New · form · 13,500 · 2
*T3:* New · whatsapp · 82,000 · 2 and 3
*T4:* New · standing · 95,000 · 1 and 3
*T5:* On hold · form · 9,000 · Fallback
*T6:* Cancelled · whatsapp · 40,000 · None (filtered)

Put these six rows in Orders with tomorrow's date and *Run once*. The small counts on each module show how many bundles reached it: Deliveries 2, Reminder 2, Alert 2, Needs checking 1.

*Step 6 · Count the credits*

- *1* credit: the search
- *7* credits: the modules at the end of routes (2 + 2 + 2 + 1)
- *0* credits: the filter and router

8 credits a night for six orders. At 30 orders a night, roughly 40 credits: about 1,200 a month, more than the Free plan's 1,000, so at that volume Tolu needs a paid plan. One search a day is far cheaper than polling every 15 minutes.

*Why this approach works*

- Junk (cancelled orders) is dropped before the router, for free.
- Each route has one job, described in words.
- Additive routes fit reality: some orders need two actions.
- The fallback turns surprises into a list, not silence.

*Common mistakes to avoid*

- Assuming a bundle takes only the first matching route.
- Two routes doing the same job (double rider entries).
- Text comparison on a number field for the ₦50,000 check.
- Expecting routes to join back for a shared last step.

*Glitch hunt*

*Glitch:* I rebuilt the 8 p.m. run for a friend's bakery. Five complaints. Explain each.

*A:* Route 1: status = Paid. Route 4: status = Paid AND total > 50000, both adding to the rider list. · Big paid orders appear twice on the rider list.
*B:* Filter: status Equal to "Paid" (case sensitive). · Orders typed "paid" never reach the riders.
*C:* Big-order filter uses Text: Greater than "50000". · A ₦9,000 order triggers the big-order alert.
*D:* No fallback route. · An "On hold" order vanishes: no rider, no reminder, no record.
*E:* A "Log to Activity" step placed only after route 3. · Only big orders are logged.

cards.prompt: Made your call on each one? Tap Reveal to check.
cards.answer:
*A:* two routes share the same job. Keep one rider-list route; let the big-order route only alert.
*B:* use the case-insensitive operator, or better, a dropdown in the sheet (0.4) so the value is always "Paid".
*C:* text comparison compares characters, and "9000" sorts after "50000". Use the numeric operator.
*D:* add a fallback route that records unexpected cases.
*E:* routes don't merge back. Log before the router, or add the log step to every route.

cards.title: Bronze (+25 XP): A filter with an OR group
cards.body:
- In your 2.1 scenario, add a filter on the link before the email: continue only if total > 20000 *OR* the customer is VIP.
- Test with four rows covering every combination.

*Done when:*
- Exactly the three rows that meet at least one condition send an email.

cards.title: Silver (+50 XP): Build and pass the 8 p.m. run
cards.body:
- Build the solved scenario with all four routes and the cancelled filter.
- Load the six test rows and run once.
- Screenshot the module counts (no personal data visible) and compare with the expected routes.

*Done when:*
- Counts match (2, 2, 2, 1), T6 stops at the filter, and nothing appears twice on the rider list.

cards.title: Gold (+100 XP): A shared ending without duplication
cards.body:
- Add a requirement: every order processed tonight must be written to an Activity tab with the routes it took.
- Solve it without copying the log module into every route. (Hint: log before the router with the routes it _will_ take, calculated with `if()` formulas from 2.2.)
- Explain in three sentences why your design is easier to maintain.

*Done when:*
- Every non-cancelled order has exactly one Activity row listing its routes correctly.

cards.q: Where do filters live in Make?
cards.why: Click any connection line to add a filter. It costs no credits.

cards.q: A bundle passes the filters of routes 2 and 3. What happens?
options: It goes down both, one after the other
cards.why: Every route whose filter passes receives the bundle.

cards.q: When does the fallback route receive a bundle?
options: Only when the bundle passed no other route
cards.why: It's the 'none of the above' route.

cards.q: A ₦9,000 order triggers a "greater than 50000" filter. Why?
options: A text operator was used instead of a numeric one
cards.why: Text comparison goes character by character. Use numeric operators for numbers.

cards.q: Every route needs the same final logging step. What's the cleanest design?
options: Add a second router at the end
cards.why: Routes don't merge in Make; shared work belongs before the split.

cards.body:
*Remember this*

1. Filters sit on links, cost nothing, and stop bundles early.
2. A bundle takes every route whose filter it passes; the fallback takes the rest.
3. Decide whether routes are exclusive or additive, and write each rule in words.
4. Use numeric operators for numbers and case-insensitive ones for text.
5. Routes never merge: do shared work before the router.
6. A daily search is often cheaper than frequent polling.

*Lesson 2.3 complete!* _Routers & Filters_ is done and saved to your progress, on WhatsApp and in the app.

Next up: Lesson 2.4, _Iterators & Aggregators_.
